en_title: Bournemouth and Sunderland Secure Carabao Cup Quarter‑Final Spots
hi_title: Bournemouth Secure Carabao Cup Quarter‑Final Spot with 3‑0 Win Over Aston Villa; Sunderland Edge Brentford 3‑2 to Reach Last Eight
en_body:
## Bournemouth Dominates Aston Villa 3‑0

Bournemouth continued its impressive run of form with a comprehensive 3‑0 victory over Aston Villa at the Vitality Stadium, securing a place in the Carabao Cup quarter‑finals for the first time in eight seasons. The Cherries opened the scoring in the seventh minute when a fine team move saw Amine Adli fire home from close range after a lofted cross from Julio Soler. Bournemouth’s captain, Lewis Cook, doubled the lead early in the second half with a low, in‑swinger from a short corner, and Álvaro Rodríguez sealed the win with a composed finish into the bottom‑right corner after Tyler Adams intercepted a loose pass.

Villa, five‑time League Cup winners, struggled to create clear chances and were denied several opportunities by goalkeeper Marco Bizot. Substitutes Alejandro Garnacho and Alysson tested the home defence, but Bournemouth’s back line kept a fifth consecutive clean sheet, easing into the last eight where they will travel to Anfield to face Liverpool.

## Sunderland Holds Off Brentford in a 3‑2 Thriller

At the Stadium of Light, Sunderland produced a late surge to beat Brentford 3‑2, with Chemsdine Talbi, Timur Tutierov and Malick Fofana on target. The home side fell behind early as Brentford’s Nathan Collins headed a free kick into the arms of goalkeeper Melker Ellborg, leading to a rebound that Michael Kayode directed against the post. Sunderland responded through a swift counter‑attack, with winger Jocelin Ta Bi setting up Tutierov for the equaliser.

Ta Bi was involved in the second goal as well, crossing to Fofana for a header into the top corner. Brentford pulled one back just before half‑time through Callum Wilson, who tapped in from close range after a scuffed shot. The visitors pressed for an equaliser in the second half, with Igor Thiago’s header eventually slipping under Ellborg to cause a late scare, but Sunderland held on.

The win marks Sunderland’s first appearance in the competition’s quarter‑finals since they were a League One team five years ago. They will now travel to Crystal Palace for their next tie.

## Impact on the Competition

Both Bournemouth and Sunderland have progressed to the last eight, joining the remaining eight clubs that will be drawn in a tie scheduled for the week commencing 14 December. The fixtures will be determined by the Carabao Cup draw, which will be broadcast on the competition’s official channels. Bournemouth’s path now includes a visit to Liverpool, while Sunderland faces Crystal Palace, setting up two high‑profile ties that promise further drama.

## What’s Confirmed and What Remains Unknown

**Confirmed**
- Exact match results: Bournemouth 3‑0 Aston Villa; Sunderland 3‑2 Brentford.
- Goal scorers and key match events as detailed above.
- Dates for the quarter‑final ties: week of 14 December.
- Venues for the next round: Bournemouth at Liverpool ( Anfield ), Sunderland at Crystal Palace (Selhurst Park).

**Uncertain**
- The full draw results that will determine which quarter‑final pairings are made.
- Any potential fixture congestion or scheduling adjustments that may arise from the draw.

## How Readers Can Verify the Information

The complete match reports and official announcements are available on the Guardian’s coverage of the Carabao Cup fourth‑round ties: [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/28/carabao-cup-fouth-round-bournemouth-aston-villa-sunderland-brentford](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/28/carabao-cup-fouth-round-bournemouth-aston-villa-sunderland-brentford). Readers can cross‑check the goal details, player performances, and the scheduled dates for the upcoming quarter‑final week.

## Practical Takeaways for Fans

- **Ticket availability**: With two local clubs advancing, fans should monitor official club websites for ticket releases for the upcoming fixtures at Anfield and Selhurst Park.
- **Broadcast details**: The Carabao Cup quarter‑final draw will be streamed on the competition’s official YouTube channel, providing live updates for scheduling.
- **Team news**: Both Bournemouth and Sunderland are likely to rotate squads for the next round, offering opportunities for younger players to impress.

This round of the Carabao Cup has set the stage for two compelling knockout ties, adding to the excitement of the domestic cup season.

## Carabao Cup Round‑of‑16 Results – A Double Header of Late‑Night Drama

The Carabao Cup fourth round delivered two contrasting stories on Tuesday night. At the Vitality Stadium, Bournemouth thrashed Aston Villa 3‑0 to book a place in the competition’s quarter‑finals for the first time in eight seasons, while at the Stadium of Light Sunderland produced a three‑goal burst in a ten‑minute spell to defeat Brentford 3‑2 and become the competition’s latest last‑eight entrant.

## Bournemouth’s Clinical Performance

Marco Rose’s Cherries opened the scoring in the seventh minute through winger Amine Adli, who finished a fine team move after a lofted cross from full‑back Julio Soler. The goal set up a fifth consecutive win across all competitions for Bournemouth. The captain, Lewis Cook, doubled the lead early in the second half with a low, in‑swinger from a short corner, and Álvaro Rodríguez sealed the win in the 69th minute, converting a rebound after Tyler Adams intercepted a loose pass.

Villa, five‑time League Cup winners, struggled to create clear chances. Their unfamiliar lineup saw goalkeeper Marco Bizot make a crucial save to deny Ben Gannon‑Doak, and substitute Alysson missed a late header. Bournemouth’s defence kept a fifth clean sheet in a row, and the result means they will travel to Anfield to face Liverpool in the quarter‑finals.

## Sunderland’s Late‑Night Surge

Régis Le Bris’s Sunderland started the match strongly, taking a 3‑0 lead by the 33rd minute. Chemsdine Talbi, Timur Tutierov and Malick Fofana were on target, with winger Jocelin Ta Bi involved in all three goals. The home side’s dominance was threatened when Callum Wilson pulled one back within three minutes, tapping in off the bar after a scuffed shot from Vitaly Janelt.

The match stretched into five minutes of added time after Igor Thiago’s header appeared to have crossed the line but was cleared by the goalkeeper Melker Ellborg. Despite a late scare when Thiago’s header slipped under Ellborg, Sunderland held on. The victory marks their first appearance in the last eight of the Carabao Cup in five years, a period when they were still a League One club.

## Brentford’s Fight Ends in Disappointment

Brentford, who started strongly with a free header from captain Nathan Collins and a Michael Kayode effort that rattled the post, could not convert their early pressure into a goal. Mamadou Sangaré’s volley was tipped over the bar by Ellborg, and later attempts from Jannik Schuster and Dango Ouattara missed the target. The Bees’ hopes of a comeback were extinguished by Sunderland’s clinical finishing.

## What Readers Can Verify

The official match reports and statistics are available on the Premier League’s website and the Carabao Cup’s official page. Detailed event timelines, player appearances and goal videos can be cross‑checked against the source article at [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/28/carabao-cup-fouth-round-bournemouth-aston-villa-sunderland-brentford).

## Practical Implications

* **Bournemouth** – The win continues a positive run for the Cherries, who will now face Liverpool, a top‑four side, in the quarter‑finals. Their defensive solidity (five clean sheets) suggests they can pose a problem for any opponent, but they will need to improve their final third efficiency to compete against a side of Liverpool’s quality.

* **Sunderland** – The victory marks a significant milestone for the club, highlighting their rapid progression from League One to challenging Premier League sides. Their ability to score quickly and defend resolutely will be key when they travel to Crystal Palace, another team looking to make a cup impact.

* **Fans & Fantasy Managers** – Both matches featured multiple goal scorers and a high‑tempo attacking style, offering plenty of fantasy points. The quarter‑final draw will be made later this week, but the two new qualifiers (Bournemouth vs Liverpool and Sunderland vs Crystal Palace) are already set for the week commencing 14 December.

* **Verification** – Readers can confirm the scores, goal scorers and line‑ups by checking the match pages on the official Premier League and Carabao Cup websites, as well as the published article linked above.

The Carabao Cup continues to deliver unexpected storylines, with Bournemouth and Sunderland both securing historic progression into the competition’s knockout phase.
